## Level 1

### Counter
Print the numbers 1 through 5 using a `while` loop.

```pyodide

```

:::{.callout-hint}
:::{.callout-note title="Hint" collapse="true"}
Use a variable to keep track of how many times you've printed so far.
:::
:::

:::{.callout-tip title="Solution" collapse="true"}
```{pyodide}
num = 0
while num < 5:
  num += 1          # this is the same as num = num + 1
  print(num)
```
:::


### Powers of 2
Use a while loop to add progressively bigger numbers together until the sum reaches or exceeds 30.  

i.e. add 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + ... until the sum is 30 or larger

> **Bonus**: at the end of the code, print the actual equation and result like:
`1 + 2 + 3 = 6`

```pyodide

```

:::{.callout-hint}
:::{.callout-note title="Hint" collapse="true"}
You'll need more than 1 variable for this one.
:::
:::

:::{.callout-hint}
:::{.callout-note title="Hint for bonus" collapse="true"}
You can keep adding things to a string like:
```python
my_name = my_name + " Bond"
```
or, using an f-string:
```python
my_name = f"{my_name} Bond"
```
:::
:::

:::{.callout-tip title="Solution" collapse="true"}
```{pyodide}
number = 1              # the first number we'll add is 1
sum = 0                 # the sum starts out at zero
equation = ""           # start with an 'empty' string, and then add onto it

while sum < 30:
  sum = sum + number    # update our sum

  # Bonus: add "+ number" onto our string version of the equation. To avoid
  # starting with a +, we handle the first time differently:
  if equation == "":    # this will be True the very 1st time we go through this loop
    equation = f"{number}"
  else:
    equation = f"{equation} + {number}"

  number = number + 1

print(f"{equation} = {sum}")
```
:::
